axis_coverage.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axis_coverage.assessment: All R1–R6 and original negatives are individually traced below, as are every operative clause of the released draft. Microphone/local/component scope survives; no fabricated test, automatic fallback, universal compatibility requirement or upload service introduced.

axis_coverage.name: Consequential source claims and conditions
axis_coverage.assessment: Primary governing API text, released browser history, original immutable Chromium source, library README/issues and independent version-pinned browser source inspected. Correct units, API operations, defaults, build/OS conditions and output-vs-hardware distinctions survive. Ogg and newer-codec exceptions are separately diagnosed; final promises remain bounded.

axis_coverage.name: Useful discovery, alternatives, history and opportunity breadth
axis_coverage.assessment: Substantive discovery goes beyond caution: native baseline, Worklet/worker/WAV, WebCodecs/muxing, established native-PCM/EBML analog, released format history, failure histories, buffer arithmetic and timer/visibility mechanism. Alternatives and conditions remain useful in final. Nonexhaustive OS/format coverage and unselected dependency/oracle are stated limits.

axis_coverage.name: Wrong criticism/corrections/rejections and exact plan dispositions
axis_coverage.assessment: All five findings independently adjudicated; F1/F2/F4/F5 are supported, F3 has an incorrect recording premise. Final acceptance of F3 is qualified to unconfirmed exploratory probes, so wrong criticism is retained as lineage rather than hidden. All exact plan clauses retained/corrected/qualified without lost scope; independently-playable chunks were falsely attributed as a user assumption.

axis_coverage.name: Supported meaning across discovery/draft/critique/final
axis_coverage.assessment: Lifecycle, local privacy, native/worklet comparison, resource bounds, assembly, capability uncertainty, histories and proposed-validation meaning are retained. Final adds truthful strict acceptance and current Safari target. Corrected draft defects remain visible; wrong Ogg criticism and stale metadata are not erased or mistaken for agreement-based proof.

axis_coverage.name: Proposed/executed validation and oracle applicability
axis_coverage.assessment: No browser/microphone/executable validation claimed; all six discriminating check groups remain proposals in a five-lane matrix. Header/channel/rate, actual MIME, complete playback/open, active-clock/event-order and byte/queue oracles are appropriate to their operations. Strict-duration accuracy still needs demonstrated per-format implementation; final explicitly rejects unverifiable output rather than certifying it.

limitations.title: Wrong Ogg criticism accepted in lineage
limitations.assessment: Critic F3 asserts a recording operation not announced by its source and calls its absence material. Final retains acceptance rhetoric but limits the candidates to exploratory unconfirmed strings. This is an unrejected lineage error and imprecise candidate provenance, not a final supported-export promise. Current Safari Ogg recording remains unobserved; pinned non-Safari source cannot establish a current binary denial.

limitations.title: Dated recording-draft probe exception omitted
limitations.assessment: Investigator explicitly uses isTypeSupported to filter candidates. The very dated source it cites deprecates this synchronous probe and distinguishes its newer-codec check from construction; ALAC/AAC/Vorbis identifiers fall outside its exposed list. Neither critique nor final map records that exception. Final removes the explicit filter, requires independent gates, says an operation failure cannot decide another operation, and makes no confirmed codec-support claim. Chrome155 source still uses a common support function for probe/constructor, so draft semantics are not claimed as observed current Chrome behavior. This leaves a useful source-condition limitation, not an established final lost-capability decision.

limitations.title: One correction is attributed to the user without support
limitations.assessment: The original plan concatenates chunks; it never claims each chunk is independently playable. Final calls that a corrected draft assumption. R4 itself does require avoiding that claim, so the technical boundary is right but the attribution is inaccurate. No requested behavior is lost.

limitations.title: Bounded matrix is deliberately partial
limitations.assessment: Safari27 also ships on macOS27; final selects macOS26/15 lanes. October7 Chrome156 early-stable rollout coexists with the ordinary155 lane. The source snapshot/analog can form exact WebM PCM candidates, though final conservatively leaves PCM offerings unselected. These are opportunity/coverage limits; brief does not require all OS builds or every format, and final never claims exhaustive coverage.

limitations.title: Runtime acceptance oracles and optional implementation are unselected
limitations.assessment: Exact duration verifier, trim/remux, encoder/library, format/quality order and current binary MIME matrix remain open. Final specifies concrete discriminating cases and refuses unverifiable/noncompliant output; it does not replace actual validation with source agreement. A plan with those explicit external choices passes semantic scope, while no implementation or compatibility certification follows.

Owner acceptance and implementation remain openly external; this is a plan, not a completed deployment.

Critic says Safari 18.4 announced Ogg recording. Governing release pages announce generic Ogg media support separately from explicit WebM MediaRecorder support; pinned Cocoa recorder source also lacks Ogg. Final does not repeat Ogg-recording success: strings are exploratory and require all gates. The false criticism was not expressly rejected. Two extra exploratory probes do not impose a recording capability or remove a requested feature.
Safari 14.1 API history is true; original discovery/draft lacked the corresponding source ID. Final adds C02 and keeps it historical.
